time-to-live (TTL) expiry for cached items. The cache is fully thread-safe
using reentrant locks, and includes a comprehensive pytest test suite.

- LRU eviction policy based on access recency

- Thread-safe operations with RLock
- Size-based eviction when cache exceeds capacity
- Automatic cleanup of expired entries
- Hit/miss statistics tracking
- Optional callback on eviction
- Serialization support for cache state

Design decisions:
- Uses OrderedDict for O(1) LRU operations
- Reentrant lock allows recursive access patterns
- Lazy expiry cleanup to avoid performance overhead
- Items are checked for expiry on access
- Eviction removes least recently used items first
"""

import threading
import time
from collections import OrderedDict
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional, TypeVar, Generic, List, Tuple, Dict, Set, Union, cast

K = TypeVar('K')
V = TypeVar('V')


class LRUCache(Generic[K, V]):
    """
    A thread-safe LRU cache with TTL expiry support.

    This cache combines the LRU eviction policy with time-to-live expiry.
    When the cache reaches its capacity, the least recently used items are
    evicted to make room for new entries. Each cached item has a TTL, after
    which it is considered expired and will be removed on next access.

    Attributes:
        capacity: Maximum number of items the cache can hold.
        Defaults to 128 if not specified.
        Must be a positive integer.

    ttl: Default time-to-live for all cached items in seconds.
        Defaults to 300 seconds (5 minutes).
        Items can override this per-entry.

    get_hits: Number of successful cache hits.
    get_misses: Number of cache misses (including expired items).

    current_size: Current number of items in the cache.

    expiry_callback: Optional callable invoked when an item is evicted
        or expires. Receives (key, value, expiry_time) tuple.

    lock: Reentrant lock ensuring thread safety for all operations.
